<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Yann" />{{rh||I ÂRA''N''YAKA, 3 ADHYÂYA, 8 KHA''ND''A, 8.|185}}{{rule}}</noinclude><section begin="aranyaka1 adhyaya3" />become twenty-five. The trunk is the twenty-fifth, and Pra''g''âpati is the twenty-fifth. There are ten fingers on his hands, ten toes on his feet, two legs, two arms, and the trunk the twenty-fifth. He adorns that trunk as the twenty-fifth. Now this day consists of twenty-five, and the Stoma hymn of that day consists of twenty-five: it becomes the same through the same. Therefore the two, the day and the hymn, are twenty-five. This is the twenty-fifth with regard to the body.

4. Next, with regard to the deities: The eye, the ear, the mind, speech, and breath, these five deities (powers) have entered into that person (purusha), and that person entered into the five deities. He is wholly pervaded there with his limbs to the very hairs and nails. Therefore all beings to the very insects are born as pervaded (by the deities or senses)<ref>The commentator takes this in a different sense, explaining atra, there, as the body pervaded by the person, yet afterwards stating that all beings are born, pervaded by the senses.</ref>.

5. This has been declared by a ''Ri''shi (Rv. X, 114, 8):—

6. 'A thousandfold are these fifteen hymns;'—for five arise from ten<ref>The commentator explains ukthâ, hymns, as members or organs. They are the five, and they spring from the ten, i.&nbsp;e. from the five elements (earth, water, fire, wind, and ether), forming part of the father and mother each, and therefore called ten, or a decade. Da''s''ata''h'' is explained by bhÛtada''s''akât.</ref>.

7. 'As large as heaven and earth, so large is it;'—verily, the self (''g''îvâtman) is as large as heaven and earth.

8. 'A thousandfold are the thousand powers<ref>The application of the senses to a thousand different objects.</ref>;'—
